recalculation.notes: The source prints both reduced post-heating pressures but not the paired ruby wavelength or Pt lattice measurement, so the pressure reduction cannot be rerun independently.

assessment.basis: The source construction is not a regression: recovered V0 is held fixed, K0-prime=4 is assumed, and the only compressed observation determines K0 algebraically. The article has no supplement, and the audit found no associated repository series; the complete reported endpoint evidence is bundled, but it leaves zero independent residual degrees of freedom.

scientific_validation.note: Validated against the free-access publisher PDF; LitCurate was used only for discovery and enumeration. Retained as the source-reported historical endpoint curve, but later multi-point CaTi2O4-type EOS measurements are preferred for quantitative use.

primary_source_check.finding: Runs 3 and 4 establish a higher-pressure MgAl2O4 phase with CaTi2O4-type Cmcm structure. The authors construct its second-order Birch curve by fixing recovered V0, assuming K0'=4, and calculating K0 from the one usable compressed run-4 cell; run-2 CaTi2O4-type peaks were too weak and overlapped for a reliable cell volume.

primary_data_check.finding: The complete observations used by the source construction are bundled from printed pressure and lattice values. There is exactly one informative finite-pressure state; the source reports no supplementary materials, and the audit found no associated repository series.

independent_refit.method: Analytical reproduction of the source's one-point construction: fixed recovered V0, K0'=4 implicit in BM2, and K0 equal to the normalized pressure of the rounded high-pressure lattice product.
independent_refit.finding: The analytically reconstructed K0 differs from the published value by 0.40 GPa because the printed axes are rounded. Applying the same calculation to the ruby/Pt pressure bracket gives a 2.89 GPa half-range, reproducing the published +/-3 GPa uncertainty after rounding; there is no independent regression residual test.

parameter_provenance.determination_method: Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Experimental method; Table 1; Sections 3.2-3.3; Table 2; Figure 4.
parameter_provenance.equation: Section 3.3: Birch second-order finite-strain EOS with Eulerian strain and K0'=4.
parameter_provenance.V0: Section 3.3 and Table 2: 240.3(4) A3 for the recovered CaTi2O4-type conventional cell, Z=4.
parameter_provenance.K0: Section 3.3: 206(+/-3) GPa, calculated as the normalized pressure of the single in-situ run-4 state after holding the separately measured V0 fixed.
parameter_provenance.implicit_K0_prime: Second-order Birch finite strain fixes K0'=4; it is assumed rather than fitted or stored as a BM2 parameter.
parameter_provenance.construction_states: Recovered run-4 zero-pressure cell fixes V0; the in-situ run-4 cell at the mean post-heating pressure of 64.3 GPa then determines K0 algebraically. Run 3 establishes phase identity but has no usable in-situ volume. This is not a regression fit.
parameter_provenance.uncertainties: The source says bulk-modulus uncertainty is calculated from the difference between ruby- and Pt-derived post-heating pressures; no covariance or confidence convention is published.

methods.scope: 300 K Table 3 pressures. The Tsuchiya-Kawamura electronic thermal correction mentioned for heated experiments is not a thermal MgAl2O4 EOS.

recalculation.notes: Table 3 gives pressures but no paired Pt volumes or lattice parameters; no raw calibrant observations are invented.

assessment.basis: Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.
qualifications: All 14 Table 3 rows, including two recovered ambient cells. Source weights and selection are unspecified; zero-rounded volume errors preclude using those errors as weights. The unweighted diagnostic recovers the printed coefficients; the dedicated Ono reproduction documents the sensitivity to excluding ambient cells.

fit.solver_message: Both `ftol` and `xtol` termination conditions are satisfied.

scientific_validation.note: Primary version-of-record PDF reviewed, with visual checks of pp. 203-204; published coefficients retained independently of diagnostic refits.

primary_source_check.finding: Source-owned 300 K BM2, V0=238.9(9) A3 and K0=219(6) GPa with K0-prime=4; distinct from Funamori (1998) and from citation-only MORB curves.

primary_data_check.finding: All 14 Table 3 rows are retained, including both recovered ambient cells. No row-resolved pressure errors or Pt volumes are printed. Parentheses are described only as errors, with no confidence convention. Printed (0) errors are preserved as rounding to zero, not exact observations. Weighting and any exclusion of recovered cells from the original regression are unspecified. The independent diagnostic uses unweighted pressure residuals, with an explicitly labeled high-pressure-only sensitivity fit.

independent_refit.method: Unweighted pressure residuals for all 14 Table 3 rows; independent printed BM2 equation, free V0 and K0. Source weighting and selection unspecified.
independent_refit.finding: Both coefficients recover the published values within their printed errors. Excluding the two ambient rows shifts K0 to 241.53 GPa; this sensitivity is documented without changing the published record.
